thesis: The PL case is grounded mainly in primary filings: revenue, RPO/backlog, customer concentration, liquidity, SBC, capex, ATM issuance and convertible debt are directly traceable to the FY2026 10-K and FY2027 10-Qs. Evidence quality is strong enough for IC, but three interpretation risks must remain explicit: reported FCF is not owner FCF after SBC/dilution, RPO/backlog are related demand measures rather than independent proofs, and the frozen net-cash/share input uses a slightly different share/debt convention from other per-share fields.

evidence.claim: FY2026 revenue, NDR, recurring ACV, operating cash flow and internal-control disclosures are directly supported by the filed FY2026 Form 10-K.
FY2027 Q2 revenue, RPO/backlog, customer concentration, cash/investments, convertible notes, H1 cash flow, SBC and ATM issuance are directly supported by the Sep. 3 Form 10-Q.
evidence.source: Uploaded PL FY2027 Q2 Form 10-Q filed 2026-09-03

evidence.claim: The Sep. 3 8-K earnings release supports FY2027 guidance, recurring ACV, Pelican/Tanager deployment and agentic-AI beta commentary.
evidence.value: FY27 revenue guide $430M-$441M; capex $100M-$115M; recurring ACV 98%

evidence.claim: The Moonshot market-cap gate is deterministic: frozen $16.99 price multiplied by latest outstanding shares yields about $6.18B, well below the $20B limit.
The strongest negative evidence—H1 SBC $33.5M, Q2 ATM issuance, warrant proceeds and customer concentration—is also primary-source supported rather than inferred from price action.

counterevidence: The $16.99 frozen price is from secondary historical-price sources rather than an exchange or issuer filing.
Reported FCF and adjusted EBITDA are useful operating measures but do not deduct SBC as an owner cost and can be affected by working-capital timing.
RPO and backlog overlap economically, so they should not be counted as two independent confirmations of demand quality.

Frozen net cash/share subtracts convertible carrying amount and uses latest outstanding shares, while some other per-share analysis uses diluted weighted-average shares; the difference is small but definitions should be standardized.
unknowns: Normalized owner FCF after working-capital reversal, SBC and full fleet replacement capex.
Maintenance versus growth capex by satellite generation.
Long-run net dilution after sustainable positive FCF is reached.
Gross retention, CAC/payback and segment-level unit economics.
Economic contribution of AI products versus core imagery and sovereign contracts.
falsifiers: Primary filings show that recurring demand or cash conversion is materially weaker than represented in the current digest after KPI definitions are normalized.
Owner FCF/share fails to improve over multiple years once working-capital timing and dilution are normalized.
KPI definitions change in a way that breaks comparability without adequate reconciliations.

key_kpis.name: Normalized owner FCF/share
key_kpis.threshold: Positive after normalizing working capital, SBC and dilution; should compound faster than share count

key_kpis.name: Net dilution
key_kpis.threshold: Trend toward low-single-digit annual growth or less after FCF breakeven

key_kpis.name: Recurring demand conversion
key_kpis.threshold: NDR/recurring ACV remain strong while RPO converts to revenue and gross profit

next_checks: Standardize share-count and convertible conventions in the next frozen snapshot.
Build an explicit reported-FCF to owner-FCF/share bridge each quarter.
Track RPO/backlog conversion without double-counting overlapping demand measures.
